common_name: Spring Bouquet Pittosporum (Compact Fragrant Mock Orange)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil; this long-established dwarf sport of Japanese pittosporum stays noticeably smaller and denser than the species without regular shearing.

directions: Site in full sun to considerable shade in fertile, well-drained soil; this mock orange tolerates heat, humidity, and occasional drought once established, and is widely planted across the Gulf South and coastal Southeast as a low-maintenance foundation and hedge shrub. Spring Bouquet holds thick, glossy, rounded leaves on a naturally compact, mounded frame smaller than the straight species, and produces clusters of small creamy-white flowers in spring with a strong orange-blossom fragrance that carries well beyond the plant itself. It responds well to shearing into a formal hedge or can be left loosely mounded for an informal screen, and rarely suffers serious pest or disease problems in well-drained soil. Protect it from hard freezes at the colder edge of its range, since foliage can suffer damage below the mid-teens.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
